exposure: Receiving delivery care at open public services
Receiving delivery care at private institutions
Parity of three or more children
cohort: The study participants were 1330 women aged 12-49 who had their last live birth within five years prior to the ENSANUT 2021 survey in Mexico.
finding: The study identified various sociodemographic, reproductive, maternal care, and health-related characteristics associated with the prevalence of planned and emergency cesarean births in Mexico.
mod_finding: Younger age, indigenous language, and public delivery care were negatively associated with any cesarean birth, while private care and hypertension increased the odds for both planned and emergency cesareans; tertiary education and lower parity were associated with emergency and planned cesareans respectively.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from the ENSANUT 2021 survey, examining live-births that occurred within five years prior to the survey.
